head: 560d7e1aab66404d7f9581b0268f622da58e08b7
author: Tandem
overview: Tandem runs AI workers that report back when they finish a task. This PR fixes three ways that loop could get stuck: finished work was rejected when a worker reworded its to-do list, workers were blocked from running the project's own checks, and a job could start twice after another coordinator took it over.

flow.title: Before / after
flow.subtitle: One implementer run, from launch to its report being accepted

changes.title: Steps match by number
changes.why: Claude Code workers paraphrase to-do subjects, so exact-text matching rejected finished reports.

steps.title: Step items carry their number
steps.note: The brief asks for `1. step text` verbatim; `stepItem` is the one place that format lives.

steps.title: A number wins over wording
steps.note: A numbered item closes the step with that number regardless of text; unnumbered items compare normalized text.

steps.title: The rejection quotes exact items
steps.note: The worker is told the exact item text to use, number included, so its next try matches.

steps.title: Worker uses the shared message
steps.note: The inline rejection string moves into `progress.ts`.

changes.title: Implementers may run pinned checks
changes.why: Refusing the pinned command stopped implementers catching a failing gate before reporting; it never counted as evidence anyway.

steps.title: Guard drops the shell refusal
steps.note: Only the reviewer refusal remains in the tool guard chain.

changes.title: Only the claim owner launches
changes.why: A taken-over operation could be launched by its old owner, leaving the task scouting with no worker.

steps.title: Return unless we own the claim
steps.note: The admitting coordinator stops when another has taken the operation over.

steps.title: Regression test
steps.note: Two controllers race one dispatch; only the new owner appends the job.

comments.body: A numbered item whose text names a different step (`3. Reuse check` when step 3 is `Run tests`) now closes step 3. Is that trade intended, or should a numbered item also need a loose text match?
This return is silent. A timeline event here would make a takeover visible in `tandem trace` instead of looking like a stall.
This string is 300+ characters on one line; splitting the two sentences would read better in the source.
The test name is great. Consider asserting the old owner's runtime has no job too, not just the new owner's.

summary: Three focused fixes, each with a regression test. One question on numbered matching, otherwise ready.
